question: After the player enters Yellow Wind Ridge (黄风岭), in what order did they defeat the following bosses? 1. Tiger Vanguard (虎先锋) 2. Yellow Wind Sage (黄风大圣) 3. Little Li Loong 4. Mother of Stones (石母) 5. Mad Tiger (疯虎) 6. The Red Loong (赤髯龙)

rollouts.answer: 4 -> 3 -> 6 -> 1 -> 5 -> 2 (Mother of Stones ~13020s, Little Li Loong ~17220s, Red Loong ~17580s, Tiger Vanguard ~18000s, Mad Tiger ~20400s, Yellow Wind Sage ~21090s)

db_evidence.notes: 5 of the 6 boss defeats (Mother of Stones, Tiger Vanguard, Red Loong, Mad Tiger, Yellow Wind Sage) are explicitly named in event_steps/episodes text near their '已击败 妖王·X' on-screen victory captions and are reliably retrievable by name search. The 6th, Little Li Loong, has NO explicit on-screen-name text anywhere in the DB at its true clue interval (17074-17236s); that fight is captioned only as 'antlered/mossy boss' / 'seated stone-like boss with crown-shaped head' inside an event_chain named 'transition to new area and antlered boss fight', immediately followed by the player entering the '藏龙洞' (hidden dragon cave). Getting Little Li Loong right therefore requires elimination reasoning (the only unnamed boss fight left once the other 5 are located) rather than a direct text match. Separately, the DB contains a distinct, explicitly-named boss '小黄龙' (Little Yellow Loong) defeated much later (~52470-52680s) whose name is textually/semantically close to the queried 'Little Li Loong' (小骊龙) and is returned as a top semantic-search hit for '小骊龙' queries, acting as a decoy.

root_causes: Entity name confusion: the DB's explicitly-named late-game boss '小黄龙' (Little Yellow Loong) is a near-homophone/near-lookalike decoy for the queried 'Little Li Loong' (小骊龙); 3 of 5 lower-scoring rollouts (2, 3, 4) took this decoy at face value and placed Little Li Loong last instead of 2nd, corrupting the whole ordering.

The true Little Li Loong defeat event in the DB carries no boss name at all (only generic visual description), so correctly answering requires elimination-by-process reasoning across all 6 named/unnamed candidates plus contextual game knowledge (entering the 'hidden dragon cave' area) -- only rollout-0 did this.

Duplicate/practice encounter confusion: an early ~16050s clip is also labeled with Tiger Vanguard-adjacent text, and rollout-1 used this early encounter instead of the later ~18000s final defeat, while rollout-0 explicitly recognized and discarded it as a duplicate.

Judge-side scoring inconsistency: rollouts 2 and 3 submitted the identical numeric order (4,6,1,5,2,3) yet received different scores (2 vs 0), indicating some judge noise independent of retrieval quality.

Visual sub-agent (clip_qa) was used in the lowest-scoring rollout (3) but only to confirm bosses that were already unambiguous from text, never directed at the actually ambiguous Little Li Loong interval, so it added no corrective value there.
what_worked: Rollout-0's strategy of first pinning down the 5 explicitly-named bosses by text/semantic search, then applying elimination over the remaining time span to identify the unnamed 6th boss, combined with rejecting the semantically-similar but distinct '小黄龙' decoy match.

Cross-checking a candidate defeat time against surrounding context (player entering '藏龙洞' hidden dragon cave right after the unnamed antlered-boss defeat) to support the Little Li Loong identification.
transferable_lessons: When a named entity from the question doesn't have an exact text match in the DB, don't accept the closest-scoring semantic-search hit uncritically -- check whether it's actually a different, textually-similar entity (e.g. 小黄龙 vs 小骊龙) before using it.

For 'order N named things' questions, first locate all N-1 unambiguous items, then apply elimination to identify the remaining one from unnamed/generic-described events in the leftover time gaps, rather than forcing a low-confidence semantic-search hit onto every named slot.

When multiple similarly-labeled encounters with the same boss name exist (e.g. an early duplicate/practice fight vs the real final defeat), prefer the one immediately followed by the '已击败' (defeated) victory-notice text/overlay, not just the first name mention.
Direct clip_qa visual-verification budget toward the genuinely ambiguous or unnamed interval, not toward bosses that already have unambiguous on-screen victory text in the retrieved rows.
open_questions: Why did the judge score two candidate answers with the identical numeric order (rollout-2: 4,6,1,5,2,3 vs rollout-3: 4,6,1,5,2,3) differently (2 vs 0) -- likely LLM-judge scoring noise, not examined further here.
